description: alarms.v2 §2.1, §2.11, §2.13 to §2.15, §5: what a tool may conclude. Computed twice by two scripts of the text's drafter that share no code, kept out of the repository, and never blessed. A case gives the owner's `presence`: "present", "absent" (a complete read without its instance token), "incomplete" (its token not seen, and the read possibly incomplete or refused) or "across_face" (across a constrained face, where presence and descriptors do not cross, and the deployment's word names alarms.v2). `descriptor`, read only when present: null when it could not be read, or {interfaces: the interface ids it lists, token: false where the alarms are in the tokenless set}; the interface token plays no part. `face`, read only across a face: {reachable: whether the deployment grants this reader a GET of the alarms}. `majors`: a descriptor's interfaces -> the major a reader reads the service's alarms by: 2, 1 (alarms.v1 and not alarms.v2), or null (neither). In every list below, expect.major is that major, null where no descriptor decides, and under 1 the case expects nothing more, alarms.v1's own conclusions.json being the evidence. `readings`: one reading of one alarm -> §5's first question (`firing`) and its last (`stale_firing`), each an answer (yes, no, unobservable, not_asked) and a reason. `latest` is the alarm's latest sample as §2.6 reads it: "firing", "resolved", "rebound" (its record replaced on its slot by another identity's, under its run, while it fired), "deleted", "undecodable", or null (the reader holds nothing of it: never read, or its record replaced or dropped). `named` is false for an unnamed alarm, asked by its slot, and changes no answer. `freshness` is freshness.v2's verdict over the slot's observations at 900 s, as freshness's own judgements.json computes them, with its reason (fresh: within_horizon; stale: beyond_horizon or no_delivery; unobservable: listened_too_short, silent, no_stamp, clock_untrusted, clock_disagrees, near_horizon, no_observation or not_a_horizon, the revision not in hand; not_asked: last_known, only an archive read), or null where nothing was observed. `lost`: the reader's subscription lost a delivery, and since then no GET has answered this slot. `previous_instance`: the latest put is attributed to an earlier instance (a snapshot under a run no present descriptor states). `held_whole`: the owner's alarms are established in this reading (§2.15). `left_out`: the read that established them listed the alarm's slot neither live nor as a tombstone, and nothing of it arrived after that read was asked; with `held_whole` it makes any held sample none, and heals `lost`. The steps are alarms.v1 §2.14's: presence (absent; presence_incomplete; face_closed), the descriptor (no_descriptor; not_listed), an archive alone (last_known), a loss (incomplete), the latest sample (deleted; resolved; rebound; not_held where established, else not_read, or nothing_crossed across a face; previous_instance), then its freshness (firing; undecodable; stale, or nothing_crossed across a face where nothing was delivered; else freshness's reason). `stale_firing` differs in three places: across a face that does not close the alarms it is unobservable, across_face; a deleted, resolved or rebound alarm, and none with the owner's alarms established, is not_asked, not_firing; and at the last step an undecodable put is unobservable, undecodable, a stale alarm yes, stale, and a fresh one no, fresh. `owner_sets`: an owner's presence, descriptor and face as above; its `read`, the reader's latest collection read of its alarms: null for none, {complete: false} for one that ended at its timeout or with an error reply, or {complete: true, snapshot}, the snapshot null where no page of it was drawn, else {complete: whether every page is held, run: "stated" (a present descriptor states it), "other" (one states another) or "unstated" (no present descriptor states a run), entries: their number}; and `since`, what its subscription saw since that read was asked: null for a reader that does not subscribe, or {lossless, present_throughout} -> whether its alarms are known whole (established, unobservable, not_asked) and the reason, the first of §2.15's order: presence and the descriptor as above; no_seed; seed_incomplete; window_lost; owner_gap (never asked across a face); snapshot_incomplete; snapshot_run (never asked across a face, nor where no run is stated); snapshot. `any_firing`: a severity `at_least`, `scope_whole` and the owners in scope, each with its set's verdict and its alarms (the first question's `answer`, and the record's `severity`, null for the escape or where none reads) -> §5's second question, in the shape of alarms.v1's conclusions.json and by its rule: an answer, a reason, `firing`, the count of alarms firing at or above the severity, and the owners counted by verdict.

majors.note: alarms.v1 listed, and not alarms.v2: read by alarms.v1's text
both listed, which breaks §2.1: a reader reads this major
alarms.v2 in the tokenless set: listed all the same
a later major alone is neither

readings.note: a firing record, fresh: its put, or a heartbeat that vouched for it, within 900 s
an unnamed alarm, the reader holding no table: answered as any other, by its slot
a firing record its owner has not confirmed within 900 s: stale, neither firing nor resolved
an unnamed alarm gone stale
a resolved record, fresh
a resolved record kept for a day: resolved whatever its age, never stale
rebound: another identity's record is on its slot under its run, so it resolved
rebound, and the slot's present record is stale: the held alarm resolved all the same
a delete, which no rule here has an owner send: alarms.v1's answer
nothing held of it, the owner's alarms established: its record was replaced or dropped, or it never fired
nothing held of it, and the owner's alarms not established
a record held, and the establishing read left its slot out: the new instance does not hold it
a resolved record held, left out by the establishing read: not_held, which is no as resolved is
a firing record an earlier instance's snapshot listed
a resolved record an earlier instance's snapshot listed: resolved comes first
an undecodable record, fresh: never at a severity or in a state
an undecodable record, stale
a delivery lost, and no GET since has answered the slot
a delivery lost, the alarm resolved before it: still incomplete, the loss may have been a re-raise
a delivery lost, and the read that then established the owner's alarms left the slot out: healed
a delivery lost, the owner's alarms established since, and the slot answered: lost is then false
freshness unobservable: listened too short
freshness unobservable: the clock not trusted
an archive alone: last-known
absent: its alarms are last-known, never firing now
absent, a resolved record held: presence comes first
its token not seen in a read possibly incomplete
the descriptor not read
the descriptor lists neither major
the descriptor lists alarms.v1 alone: alarms.v1's text reads it
the descriptor lists both: read by this text
alarms.v2 in the tokenless set: found by its descriptor, never by a token
the tokenless owner's alarm resolved
across a face that grants the GET: a firing entry, fresh by its confirmation
across a face, a firing entry past its horizon
across a face, nothing delivered
across a face, nothing read
across a face, a complete snapshot left the slot out
across a face, a resolved entry
across a face closed to the alarms: unobservable, never "not firing"
across a face closed to them, with nothing held
a firing record with nothing observed of its freshness
freshness unobservable: the revision the owner names is not in hand, so no horizon (§2.7)

owner_sets.note: a complete snapshot of three entries
a complete snapshot with no entry: the owner's word that nothing fires, at once, with no window
the same for a reader that only GETs
no read made
a read that ended at its timeout
a read that ran to its final reply and drew no page: silence, never "nothing fires"
a page of the snapshot is missing: read again
a delivery lost since the read was asked
a gap in the owner's presence since the read: a new instance may hold other alarms
a loss and a gap: the loss comes first
a loss since, and a page missing: the loss comes first
a snapshot under a run no present descriptor states: an earlier instance built it
the same for a reader that only GETs
a page missing under another run: incomplete comes first
the present descriptor states no run: nothing to compare, and the snapshot stands
absent
presence possibly incomplete
the descriptor not read
the descriptor lists neither major: not asked, and the owner is counted with those that have no alarms to ask
the descriptor lists alarms.v1 alone
alarms.v2 in the tokenless set, a complete snapshot with no entry
across a face that grants the GET, a complete snapshot with no entry: established, where alarms.v1 answered across_face for ever
across a face, a complete snapshot of three
across a face, the GET ended at its timeout
across a face, a page missing
across a face closed to the alarms: never "nothing fires"
across a face that grants the GET, none made: pushes and a heartbeat alone establish nothing
across a face, a subscriber that lost a delivery since its read
across a face, presence does not cross: a gap is not asked

any_firing.note: one owner established by a snapshot with no entry: nothing fires
a firing alarm at the severity
a firing alarm below the severity
an unnamed alarm counts: its severity is in its record
resolved and rebound alarms are no
a stale alarm at the severity: unobservable, never no
a stale alarm below the severity does not stop a no
a firing alarm whose severity is the escape: yes without a severity
an undecodable record has no severity known
one owner fires and another is unobservable: yes, whatever else is known
one owner established with nothing, another's snapshot incomplete
an owner across a face closed to its alarms: never "nothing fires"
an owner not listed is not asked, and stops no answer: the hazard of a reader that knows only one major
the reads that found the scope were not whole
a firing alarm of an owner whose alarms are not established still answers yes
two owners, three alarms at or above warning
